name: giallo
description: Rust TextMate-grammar engine aiming for VS Code-faithful highlighting

host-language.comment: Pure Rust crate (edition 2024). The repo has Node scripts, but they only generate test snapshots against vscode-textmate.

form-factor.comment: Library only. The one binary target, build-registry (behind the `tools` feature), builds the grammar/theme dump. It is not a highlighting CLI.

license.comment: EUPL-1.2 for every release since 0.1.0. A 2022 placeholder 0.0.1 was MIT. The bundled grammars and themes come from shikijs/textmate-grammars-themes and keep their upstream licences (mostly MIT).

documentation.comment: No dedicated docs site. The README and the docs.rs API reference are the documentation, plus an examples directory in the repo.

first-release.comment: First real release was 0.1.0 on 2025-12-19, announced on the Zola forum. The crate name was reserved with a 12 KB placeholder 0.0.1 (MIT) on 2022-08-18, which is not counted.

latest-version.comment: Checked 2026-11-18. Released 2026-11-04. The README install snippet still shows 0.2.0.

engine-model.comment: The tokenizer is documented as replicating microsoft/vscode-textmate's logic. Tests compare its output with vscode-textmate snapshots.

regex-engine.comment: 0.6.0 switched from a fork of rust-onig (Oniguruma C) to fancy-regex in `oniguruma_mode` (commit 'Use fancy-regex instead of onig'). The README still mentions the onig fork, which is stale. The few patterns fancy-regex can't compile are swapped for a never-matching regex.

embedded-languages.comment: TextMate external grammar includes and injections (injectTo) are resolved by `link_grammars()`. The bundled VS Code-derived html grammar embeds the css and javascript grammars, and the repo has injection snapshot tests.

language-auto-detection.comment: Content-based detection is not offered. The language must be named in HighlightOptions.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Grammar `fileTypes` are parsed but no public extension/filename lookup is exposed. Lookup is by grammar name or alias only, though some aliases match extensions (rs, py, ts, yml).

resumable-line-state.comment: The tokenizer and its rule stack are private modules. `Registry::highlight` takes the whole input string. The irosashi comparison table also lists giallo as having no per-line API.

incremental-reparsing.comment: There is no edit/reparse API. Each call re-tokenizes the full input.

semantic-distinctions.comment: TextMate grammar engine with no syntax tree. Per the guideline, regex-based recognition of definitions doesn't count.

bundled-languages.comment: 243 entries in the README's generated grammar list (master, 0.6.0), minus the 'plain' grammar. Aliases are not counted, but variant grammars (html-derivative, vue-html, fortran fixed/free, etc.) are. The README calls it '220+'. Requires the `dump` feature.

grammar-format.comment: Raw grammars are deserialized with serde_json only. Plist .tmLanguage files are not parsed and would need converting to JSON first.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes VS Code/TextMate JSON grammars directly, including the curated Shiki set. A Zola user reported adding upstream .tmLanguage.json grammars (SystemVerilog, VHDL) as long as they have a top-level name field.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Registry::add_grammar_from_path / add_grammar_from_bytes (bytes added in 0.6.0), followed by link_grammars().

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: The builtin dump (~1.1 MiB zstd bitcode) loads every grammar up front. Only regex compilation is deferred to first use (OnceLock per pattern), which is why the first use of each language is slower.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Rated 4. The grammars track upstream VS Code/Shiki grammars, and output is snapshot-tested against vscode-textmate. Users report a big improvement over syntect. Not 5 because no fidelity score is published, and since 0.6.0 the patterns fancy-regex can't compile silently never match.

bundled-themes.comment: 65 entries in the README's generated theme list (master, 0.6.0). The README says '~60'. These are Shiki's curated VS Code themes and require the `dump` feature.

theme-format.comment: Loads VS Code theme JSON (tokenColors) only. tmTheme plist is not supported.

token-classification.comment: Theme rules are matched against hierarchical TextMate scope stacks, vscode-textmate style. The scopes themselves are not exposed in the public token output, and generated CSS classes are per-style (e.g. Zola's z-l-*/z-d-*).

css-class-output.comment: HtmlRenderer::css_class_prefix switches to class output. Registry::generate_css / generate_dual_css produce the matching stylesheets.

multi-theme-output.comment: ThemeVariant::Dual { light, dark } renders once. Inline styles use CSS light-dark(), and in class mode generate_dual_css emits l-/d- prefixed stylesheets.

public-token-api.comment: Registry::highlight returns HighlightedCode, whose `tokens: Vec<Vec<HighlightedText>>` holds one vector per line. The README says it gives back 'everything you need to implement your own renderer'.

ir-kinds.comment: HighlightedText = text plus ThemeVariant<Style> (foreground, background, font_style). Scope stacks exist internally (tokenizer::Token) but are not exported.

serializable-ir.comment: Partial. docs.rs shows HighlightedText, Style and ThemeVariant implementing serde Serialize/Deserialize, so the token vectors serialize. The HighlightedCode wrapper (which borrows the compiled theme) does not.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Each token carries resolved foreground/background colours and font style (one set per theme in dual mode).

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: HighlightedText has only `text` and `style`. Lines are implied by the outer Vec, but there are no byte/char offsets. The internal Token has a byte span, but it isn't public.

custom-formatter-api.comment: There is no formatter trait. Instead, the README documents rendering the public HighlightedCode yourself, and examples/custom_rendering.rs shows a full custom HTML renderer.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Limited. RenderOptions.highlight_lines and hide_lines (line ranges) apply in both HTML and terminal renderers, and parse_markdown_fence parses Zola-style `hl_lines=`/`hide_lines=`. There are no diff/focus markers or arbitrary range decorations, and the options apply at render time rather than on the IR.

output-formats.comment: HtmlRenderer (inline styles or CSS classes) and TerminalRenderer (ANSI, documented as requiring truecolor). The README's 'one renderer' line predates the TerminalRenderer.

line-numbers.comment: RenderOptions.show_line_numbers and line_number_start. The gutter CSS is exported as GIALLO_CSS.

streaming-output.comment: highlight() tokenizes the full input, and renderers return one String. There is no line iterator API.

terminal-ready.comment: TerminalRenderer emits truecolor ANSI escapes, with line numbers and highlighted lines. With dual themes you pick one via theme_type.

native-dependencies.comment: Since 0.6.0 the regex engine is pure-Rust fancy-regex (through 0.5.x it linked Oniguruma C via a rust-onig fork). The only C code left is the zstd crate (libzstd via zstd-sys), pulled in by the optional `dump` feature that Registry::builtin() needs. Without it the crate is pure Rust.

runs-in-browser.comment: No official browser build or docs. The community 11ty-plugin-giallo compiles giallo into a Wasm component for Node, which suggests wasm32 builds are feasible, but they aren't supported first-party.

wasm-build.comment: No official WASM target or documented wasm32 support. The only WASM build found is the community 11ty plugin.

synchronous-api.comment: Plain synchronous Rust calls: Registry::builtin(), link_grammars(), highlight(), render().

bindings-ports.comment: No official bindings. Small community wrappers exist: 11ty-plugin-giallo (Eleventy, via a Wasm component) and giallo.kak (Kakoune).

core-package-size.comment: crate_size of the giallo 0.6.0 .crate on crates.io (~1.5 MB), which includes the builtin.zst grammar/theme dump (~1.1 MiB per the README).

throughput-tier.comment: fasthighlight PR #60 (reproducible scripts, competitor-authored, 2026-11-11): 21 warm snippets took giallo 0.5.2 35 ms vs syntect 5.3.0 20 ms, about 1.75x the fastest candidate. fasthighlight (Go, not a candidate) took 0.68 ms. This was measured on 0.5.2 (Oniguruma). 0.6.0 moved to fancy-regex with several perf commits and hasn't been re-measured.

initialization-cost.comment: Same benchmark (giallo 0.5.2): initialization 40–58 ms vs syntect ~1 ms. First use of each language adds lazy regex compilation (720 ms total across 27 snippets' languages, ~27 ms per language on average), so a first highlight lands at roughly 70 ms.

monthly-downloads.comment: crates.io recent_downloads (90 days) of 13,571 divided by 3, checked 2026-11-18. Mostly driven by Zola builds.

maintenance-status.comment: 12 releases between 2025-12 and 2026-11, the latest on 2026-11-04, with regular commits (regex engine swap, perf work). Pre-1.0 (0.x), so API breaks between minors are expected.

documentation-quality.comment: Rated 3. There's a solid README (usage, renderers, grammar/theme lists, rationale) and a docs.rs reference (the crate uses deny(missing_docs)), plus an examples folder. There is no guide site or migration notes, and the README is partly stale (0.2.0 install snippet, onig fork, 'one renderer').

notable-users.value: Zola (default highlighter since 0.22); sites built on Zola, e.g. the Rust blog (blog.rust-lang.org)
notable-users.comment: Zola 0.22.0 (2026-01-09) replaced syntect with giallo, and Zola's Cargo.toml depends on giallo 0.5 with `dump`. The Rust blog's Zola 0.23.6 upgrade PR (merged 2026-10-08) adjusts for giallo's CSS classes. Smaller users: 11ty-plugin-giallo and giallo.kak.

bus-factor.comment: Lives in the getzola org, but Keats (the Zola maintainer) made 77 of ~86 commits. The other 7 contributors have 1–2 commits each.
